Death Reference No. 1 of 2014. with
Criminal Appeal No. 7439 of 2013. with
Criminal Appeal No. 20 of 2014. with
Criminal Miscellneous Case No. 27020 & 35820 of 2014. with
Criminal Miscellneous Case No. 21226 of 2015.
lawyer:
Md Moniruzzaman (Rubel), Deputy Attorney-General with Mr Abul Aziz Masud, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State. 
Yahia, State Defence Lawyer—For the Condemned Prisoner. 
SM Mahbubul Islam, Advocate with Mohammad Imran Miah, Advocate—For the Appellants. [In all the appeals]
full_judgment:
ASM Abdul Mobin J : This death reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is submitted by the Judge, Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka for confirmation of sentence of death awarded upon the condemned-prisoner Kamal Miah. Learned Judge of the Tribunal convicted him under section 302 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to death in Druto Bichar Case No. 20 of 2012 arising out of Bajitpur Police Station Case No. 4 dated 5-5-2005 corresponding to GR No. 225(2)05 by judgment and order dated 18-11-2013. By the same judgment and order, learned Judge also convicted accused Doyal Mia, Anarash Mia, Shahin Mia, Shahel Mia, Prokash Mia, Rubel Mia, Abal Mia, Nurul Islam alias Sujit, Mamun Mia, Rana Sikder, Rupak and Sohel under sections 302 and 34 of Penal Code and sentenced them to suffer imprisonment for life with a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer another one year rigorous imprisonment. Out of them, accused Mamun Mia alias Mamun and Rana Sikder filed Criminal Appeal No. 20 of 2014 and accused Doyal Mia, Pi okash Mia, Abal Mia, Anarash Mia and Shahin Mia filed Criminal Appeal No. 7439 of 2013, while Rubel Mia, Shahel Mia and Sohel Mia filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 35820 of 2014, 27020 of 2014 and 21226 of 2015 respectively against the same judgment and order. The death reference, criminal appeals and miscellaneous cases are heard together and disposed of by this judgment. 

 2. The proceeding was initiated by Ms Parveen Akter (PW 11), informant and wife of the victim Md Rabiullah on lodging a first informaion report (FIR) with Bajitpur police station on 5-5- 2005. It was stated that victim Md Rabiullah contested for the post of Chairman in the Union Parishad election. Soon after the election, accused Kamal Mia started a conspiracy to kill him. On the day of occurrence, the victims along with others were going to Kishoregonj for appearing in a case before the Additional sessions Judge on 25-4-2005. The accused party some how came to know the date of their appearance in the Court. When the victim along with others were on the way to Bajitpur Railway Station, at about 7-00 pm the accused being armed with chapati, rod, cricket bat etcetera attacked them at about 200/250 cubits off to the livestock hospital. Accused Kamal, Doyal, Rubel and Nazrul Islam alias Sujit brought him down from rickshaw and took him to the northern lane, Uzzal (not sent up in the charge sheet) passed an order to kill him, when accused Kamal dealt a chapati blow on his right ear. Having received the blow he fell down on the ground and all other accused pulled him further and accused Mamun, Doyal, Rubel and Rana Sikder struck on his legs, and arms arm by rod. Accused Nazrul Islam alias Sujit gave him blows by a cricket bat. The other accused also dealt indiscriminate blows on his body. Due to their assault, he became senseless. On hearing the outcry of his companions, people rushed to the place, saw and heard about the occurrence. In the meantime the accused party left the place. He was taken to Bhagalpur Jahurul Islam Medical College Hospital and from there to PG Hospital, Dhaka. He was also taken to Holy Family Hospital, but was taken back to PG Hospital. He did not regain his sense till filing of the FIR. The informant was busy with her husband's treatment and, as such, there was a delay in lodging the FIR. 

 3. Kazi Daud Hossain, a Sub-Inspector (SI) of Police (PW 16) was assigned with the investigation, who investigated the case and submitted charge-sheet against all the accused except Uzzal Mia and Rubel Mia. The informant filed a naraji petition against, upon which further investigation was held and another Sub-Inspector of police named Md Shahjar Hossain Sharif who also submitted charge-sheet against same set of accused. After filing of 2nd charge-sheet, again an order of further investigation was passed and the case was further investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). Md Azizul Huq, a SI of Criminal Investigation Department (CID) submitted charge-sheet against all the accused except Uzzal Miah under sections 301, 302 and 34 of the Penal Code. 

 4. The case was sent to the Court of Sessions judge, Kishoregonj for trial. Learned Sessions Judge framed charge under sections 302 and 34 of the Penal Code against all the accused. The charge was read over to them, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 5. When the case was pending before the Sessions Judge Kishoregonj, it was transferred to Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka for trial. 

 6. In order to prove the charge, prosecution examined 13 witnesses. PW 1 Mohin Ahammed alias Rohan, son of the victim stated that he was at his school hostel on 25-4-2005. In the evening his uncle and a witness of the case Md Danu Miah (PW 2) went to his hostel and stated that while his father and others were going to Bajitpur Railway Station from Dilalpur Bazaar, the accused attacked him. On the order of Uzzal, Kamal gave a chapati blow on his right ear, his father fell down on the ground. Accused Mamun, Doyal, Rabiul and Rana Sikder gave rod blows on his legs and arms. Accused Nurul Islam alias Sujit struck blows on his left leg by a cricket bat. Other accused also gave indiscriminate blows on his person. When his uncle and others raised hue and cry, local people rushed to the spot. His father was taken to Bhagalpur Jahurul Islam Medical College Hospital. He having heard the occurrence went there, saw his father under treatment. His father told him that accused Kamal, Doyal, Anarosh, Shahin, Abal, Shahel, Prokash, Rubel, Uzzal, Rupak, Nurul Islam alias Sujit, Rana Sikder, Mamun, Sohel had inflicted injuries on his person. He narrated the occurrence to his mother over phone. She came to hospital and heard the occurrence from the witnesses. He further stated that he and his mother went to Bajitpur Police Station for lodging FIR, but police declined to receive it. Instead, they were told that they (Police) had instruction from their higher authority not to record their case. Two of the accused were sons of local Member of Parliament (MP) and due to his interference police refused to accept their case. He also stated that his father was taken to PG Hospital, Dhaka and from there to Holy Family Hospital. As his condition deteriorated, he was again taken back to PG hospital. At one stage, the Officer-in-Charge of Bajitpur Police Station informed them that he would accept their case, when his mother along with his uncle Nurul Mia went to the police station and lodged the FIR on 5-5-2005. 

 7. In cross-examination his attention was drawn to his previous statement which he denied. He also denied the defence suggestion that his father and uncles were accused of a murder case for killing of Mir Hussain and that the local people in retaliation of the murder of Mir Hussain attacked and killed his father. 

 9. In cross-examination PW 2 stated that they were going to appear in a dacoity case. The victim was an accused of that case. When the 1st rickshaw was intercepted, they were 4/5 cubits away. The accused dragged the victim on a lane. His (PW 2's) attention was drawn to his previous statement which he denied. He further denied the defence suggestion that he was not present at the scene of occurrence or that he did not at all see the occurrence. 

 12. PW 4 Md Nuru Mia stated that he was younger brother of the victim. He along with others started from their house to go to Dilalpur Bazaar on 25-5-2005. They saw Kalam and Doyal there to speak with someone over mobile phone. From Dilalpur Bazaar they were going to Bajititpur Railway Station by three rickshaws. The victim and Fazlu were in the 1st rickshaw, he himself was in the 2nd and Khorshed and Younus in the 3rd. When they reached in front of Farazi House at the east of livestock hospital, the accused intercepted them. They pulled down the victim and dragged him on a side lane. Thereafter on the order of Uzzal, Kamal struck him a chapatti blow on his left ear. He fell down on the ground. Then Mamun, Doyal, Rubel and Rana Sikder dealt rod blows on both his legs and arms. Accused Nurul Islam alias Sujit also gave blows on his left leg by a cricket bat. On their outcry, local people rushed to the scene of occurrence and the accused having seen them left the place. They took the victim near to a cinema hall and there from to Bhagalpur Hospital. His son Rohan was called in at the hospital. The victim disclosed the names of the accused and also narrated the occurrence to him. They heard that victim's wife went to police station on the following day, but police refused to accept her case. The victim was referred to Dhaka for better treatment. He was accordingly taken to PG Hospital Dhaka, where lie died on 5-5-2005. He and victim's wife went to police station at about 10-00 am on 5-5-2005 and lodged the FIR. 

 15. In cross-examination PW 5 stated that the 10 had examined him during investigation of the case. 

 17. In cross-examination PW 6 stated that he was a peanut hawker and an accused of Arman murder case. He saw the victim lying with bleeding injury. He made a statement to the Investigating Officer after 5/6 days of the occurrence. 

 18. PW 7 Lutfur Rahman stated that victim Rabiullah was his uncle. He was at home on 25-5-2005. Victim's son Rohan informed him over mobile phone that he (victim) was at the hospital. He along with his aunt went to the hospital and saw his uncle under treatment. His father Nuru Mia (PW 4) and others narrated the occurrence to him. On the following day his aunt went to police station to lodge a FIR, but police refused to accept her case. The victim was referred to PG Hospital Dhaka and he was taken there. Once he was taken to Holy Family Hospital, but brought back again to PG Hospital, where he died on 5-5-2005. Police came to the hospital in the afternoon on 5-5-2005, conducted inquest and prepared a report, which he signed. On recall, he proved the seized articles as material exhibits. 

 24. PW 11 Parveen Akter, informant and wife of the victim Rabiullah stated that about 8 years ago on 12 Baishak she was at her home. Her husband along with Khorshed, Danu Mia, Younus, Nuru, Fazlu went out for going to Kishoreganj. After Magrib prayer her son Rohan (PW 1) informed that accused Kamal and others assaulted his father and he was at Bhagalpur hospital. She went to hospital, talked to her son. He then told her that his father had disclosed the names of accused Kamal, Doyal, Anarash, Shahin, Abal, Sahed, Prokash, Uzzal, Rubel, Rana Sikder, Mamun, Nurul Islam alias Sujit, Rupak and Sohel and had also narrated the occurrence. his father also told him that they had assaulted him and inflicted injuries on his person. On the following day she along with her son went to police station, but the Officer-in-charge of the police station refused to accept her case saying that he had instruction from his higher authority not to record the case. She took her husband to PG Hospital and there from to Holy Family Hospital. Her husband was taken back to PG Hospital. On 21 Baishak a news was published in the paper, wherein it was stated that police would accept her case. Accordingly, she sent the FIR to police station through her brother-in-law Nuru Mia on 22nd Bhaishak. 

 25. In cross-examination PW 11 stated that she could not recollect the name of typist, who had typed the FIR. She did not mention the fact of phone call by her son in the FIR. She stated that she did not also mention the names of the persons, from whom she had heard about the occurrence, but mentioned that she heard it from the witnesses. She denied the defence suggestion that she implicated the accused in the case out of previous enmity. 

 31. PW 15 Md Ferdouse Hossain, an Inspector of Police stated that he was attached with Bajitpur police station on 5-5-2005. SI Mizanur Rahman received a written FIR and recorded the case. He himself took the charge of investigation, visited the place of occurrence, prepared a sketch-map with index, recorded statements of witnesses, seized alamats and at one stage he handed over the charge of investigation to CID on 8-5-2005. 

 34. In cross-examination PW 16 denied the defence suggestion that he did not hold the investigation properly. In his further cross-examination on recall, he stated that he had examined one rickshaw puller named Shahidullah. He did not collect any paper to show that the victim and his companions were going to appear in a case. He also stated that witness Mahin, son of the victim did not mention disclosure of names of the accused by his father in his statement recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 35. PW 17 Md Azizul Haque stated that he was given the task of investigation. He perused the case dairy and other papers and also examined the informant. The previous Investigating Officer submitted charge-sheet against 12 accused. He submitted charge-sheet against 13 accused on 15-6-2010. 

 42. Learned Deputy Attorney-General refers to the evidence of PWs 2 and 4 and submits that these two eye-witnesses described the entire occurrence from beginning to end. They attributed specific overtact to the accused. In addition, PWs 1 and 13 proved the dying declaration. Their evidence, circumstances and other evidence adduced in the case are sufficient to prove the charge against the accused. He also refers to the case of Md Abdul Mazid Sarkar vs State, 1988 BLD (AD) 71 = 40 DLR (AD) 83 and submits that mere delay of death of the victim will not reduce the degree of culpability of the accused. 

 43. Mr Yahia, learned State Defence Lawyer appearing for the condemned prisoner Kamal submits that as many as 11 eye-witnesses are named in the FIR, who claim to have seen the occurrence, but only 3 witnesses have been examined and no explanatibn whatsoever has been given for non-examination of 8 other witnesses and in absence of their evidence the prosecution case cannot be said to have been proved. He further submits that the witnesses, who are examined, are all interrelated and interested witnesses and it is not safe to convict the accused on the evidence of such interested witnesses. He lastly submits that this is not a case, where the sentence of death is appropriate, even it is assumed that the condemned prisoner is found to be involved in the occurrence. 

 44. Mr SM Mahbubul Islam, learned Advocate appearing in the appeals and criminal miscellaneous cases at the very outset submits that the dying declaration as has been claimed by the witnesses is very much doubtful. In support of his submission he refers to the FIR, which was lodged after 10 days of the occurrence. It is stated in the FIR that just after the occurrence, the informant rushed to the hospital where she came across with her son, others witnesses and heard the detail facts, but the very fact of dying declaration is not mentioned. PW 13 Md Mobarak Hossain, Head Master of the local school also deposed and narrated the dying declaration allegedly heard from the victim. Learned Advocate assails his evidence on the ground that this witness is not named in the FIR nor is he cited in the 1st and 2nd charge-sheet and his name does only appear in the 3rd charge-sheet. It is apparent that he has been introduced long after the occurrence just to strengthen the so called dying declaration. Learned Advocate further submits that the eye-witnesses, namely, PWs 2 and 4 are not at all reliable. Their presence in the scene of occurrence is equally doubtful. If they had really accompanied the victim, it is almost certain that they would have been attacked and assaulted by the accused. They did not even come forward to save the victim from the hands of the accused, which is highly improbable as such their evidence cannot be relied upon for conviction of the accused. 

 45. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the evidence and materials on record. Prosecution in order to prove the charge introduced a dying declaration through the lips of the witnesses during trial. It is PWs 1 and 3 who claim to have heard the dying declaration at the hospital immediately after the occurrence, but the dying declaration as claimed by them has not been mentioned in the FIR though it was lodged after 10 days of the occurrence. In absence of any reference of the alleged dying declaration in the FIR, it is hardly belie Jable. PW 13 was not cited as a witness in the 1st and 2nd charge-sheet. He was brought in the case long after the occurrence, if he was really a witness to the dying declaration, he could have certainly been cited in the 1st and 2nd charge-sheets. PW 1 is the son of the informant, who had every opportunity to inform his mother about the dying declaration before lodging the FIR. Since the dying declaration is not beyond doubt, reliance cannot be put on it and we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant with regard to the dying declaration allegedly made by the victim while he was under treatment in the hospital. 

 49. In this case it is crucial to determine the offence actually committed by the accused. The court below convicted accused Kamal under section 302 of the Penal Code and rest of the accused under section 302 of the Penal Code with the aid of section 34 of the Penal Code. It is true the victim died in the hospital after 10 days of the occurrence due to injuries sustained at the hands of the accused. 

 50. As the victim died due to the injuries, no doubt it is a case of homicide. Now the question is whether the homicide is amount to murder or not murder. 

 51. It is from a plain reading of section 300 of the Penal Code that if any act falls within 5 exceptions described therein is not murder and only a culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Apart from the exceptions, the difference of two offences i.e. culpable homicide not amounting to murder and murder as has been defined in sections 299 and 300 of the Penal Code may also appear if looked into the words used in those two sections. If two provisions are compared then the difference between two offences may be appreciated. In the scheme of the penal code "culpable homicide" is genus and "murder" its specie. All murder is culpable homicide but not vice versa. There is distinction between "murder" and "culpable homicide". It is generally viewed that if any case falls within any of the exceptions to section 300 is not murder, but culpable homicide not amounting to murder punishable under section 304 part I of the Penal code. If a case does not fall within any of the exceptions to section 300 of the Penal Code, even it may not be murder but culpable homicide not amounting to murder. For the offence murder, the act must come within the provisions of clause 1, 2, 3, 4 of section 300. The distinction between "murder" and "culpable homicide not amounting to murder" may escape notice if scope and meaning of the words used in various clauses of section 299 and 300 is not given to their true and real meaning. 

 52. A comparative table of the two offences was shown by Melvill, J, in the case of Govinda vs Emperor, (1876) 1 Born 342 which is referred to in so many subsequent cases. The comparative table is quoted below for appreciation of the points of distinction between the two offences: 

 54. The aforementioned clause (b) of section 299 correspondents to the clause (2) and (3) of section 300, intention to cause death is not a requirement of clause (2). It is only the intention of causing the bodily injury coupled with the offender's knowledge of the likelihood of such injury causing the death of the particular victim is sufficient to bring the killing with the ambit of this clause. Case falling in clause (2) is borne out by illustration (b) appended to section 300. Clause (b) of section 299 does not postulate any such knowledge on the part of the offender. Instances of cases falling under clause (2) of section 300 can be where the assailant causes death by a fist blow intentionally given knowing that the victim is suffering from an enlarged liver or enlarged spleen or heart disease and such blow is likely to cause death of that particular person as a result of rupture of the liver, or spleen or the failure of the heart as the case may be. If the assailant has no such knowledge about the disease or special frailty of the victim, or an intention to cause death or bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, the offence will not be murder, even if the injury which caused the death was intentionally given. 

 55. In clause (3) of section 300 instead of the words, "likely to cause death" occurring in the corresponding clause (b) of section 299, the words "sufficient in the ordinary course of nature" have been used. Obviously, distinction lies between a bodily injury likely to cause death and bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature. The word 'likely' in clause (b) of section 299 conveys the sense of probable as distinguished from a mere possibility. The words "bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death" means that the death will be the most probable result of the injury having regard to the ordinary course of nature. For case to fall within clause (3) it is not necessary that the offender intended to cause death. So long as the death ensures from the intentional bodily injury or injuries sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature. 

 57. The distinction between the two provisions of law is no doubt fine and real and if overlooked, may result in miscarriage of justice. 

 58. In the present case, accused Doyal, Mamun, Rubel, Rana Sikder and Nurul Islam alias Sujit are said to have dealt rod and cricket bat blows on the hands and legs of the victim and these injuries are not sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death of the victim. Accused Kamal gave a chapati blows on right ear of the victim but in the post-mortem examination a lacerated injury was found on right ear of the victim. Usually a lacerated injury is not caused by a sharp weapon. It is apparent that the blunt side of the chapati was used in inflicting injury on right ear of the victim. If all the injuries found on the person of the victim allegedly caused by the said accused are taken into consideration, it would be found that the injuries inflicted on the body of the victim ware not inflicted with the intention of causing death. It is also in the record that the victim died after 10 days of the occurrence. It is true that survival of the victim on account of treatment for some days will not reduce the liability or is not a ground to put a premium on the offence committed by them. The doctor who held post-mortem examination did not assign a particular injury for causing death of the victim. It is the cumulative effect of all the injuries which caused the death. Therefore, from the manner of infliction of the injuries on the victim, those found by the Doctor and the facts and circumstances of the case, it is established that the injuries inflicted with the intention of causing bodily injury as is likely to cause death and not with the intention of causing injury which is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. Therefore, the acts of the accused attracts clause (b) of section 299 of the Penal Code and they are liable for the offence punishable under section 304 Part I of the Penal Code. Although accused Kamal, Mamun, doyal, Rubel, Rana Sikder and Nurul Islam alias Sujit are liable for the offence culpable homicide not amounting to murder, their degree of culpability is not the same. Accused Mamun, Doyal, Rubel, Rana Sikder and Nurul Islam alias Sujit gave rod and cricket bat blows on the outer limb of the deceased. Their individual act is not sufficient to cause death. They are liable for the death owing to the principle of joint liability under section 34 of the Penal Code. In the circumstances justice will be met if they are given a lesser sentence under the law. 

 60. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that accused Kamal, Mamun, Doyal, Rubel. Rana Sikder and Nurul Islam alias Sujit were involved in the occurrence and the victim died due to their assault and they are liable for the offence punishable under section 304 part 1 and 34 of the penal code. 

 62. Criminal Appeal No. 7439 of 2013, so far it relates to accused Doyal and Criminal Appeal No. 20 of 2014 are dismissed. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 35820 of 2014 is discharged. The conviction of accused Doyal, Mamun, Rana Sikder, Rubel and Nurul Islam alias Sujit is altered to section 304 Part 1 and 34 of the Penal Code and they are sentenced to suffer 10 years rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Taka 10,000 each in default to suffer another one year rigorous imprisonment. They are directed to surrender to the Court below for serving out their sentence. 

 63. The Rules in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 27020 of 2014 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 21226 of 2015 are made absolute. The conviction and sentence of accused accused Anarash Mia, Shahin Mia, Shahel Mia, Prokash Mia, Abal Mia, Rupak and Sohel Mia are set-aside and they are acquitted of the charge levelled against them. They are discharged from their bail bonds.
